scientificSummary.scope: Bounded human Behçet disease overview: HLA/ERAP1 and cytokine-locus susceptibility, T-cell and neutrophil activation, NET/coagulation and endothelial injury, plus mucocutaneous, ocular, vascular, neurologic, joint and intestinal branches. Primary-report associations, culture mechanisms and intervention populations remain distinct. Excludes monogenic mimics, diagnostic criteria and comprehensive treatment guidance.

paragraphs.text: Circulating NET markers were higher in active than inactive disease and healthy donors. A selected vascular cohort included 23 Behçet patients with nonpulmonary aneurysms. Purified Behçet neutrophils exhibited spontaneous NET formation compared with healthy donors.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Abstract-level inspection; selected study population or assay, not proof of a universal disease mechanism. Selected clinical cohort; no population prevalence or molecular cause established. Treatment efficacy has not been synthesized in this summary.

after.text: US labeling indicates apremilast for adult oral ulcers associated with Behçet disease.
limitations: Adult oral-ulcer indication; does not establish protection against ocular, vascular, intestinal or CNS disease.
Target engagement is distinct from organ-specific efficacy.

after.text: In the 207-person phase 3 trial, apremilast reduced oral-ulcer burden over 12 weeks versus placebo; major-organ involvement was excluded.
limitations: No inference of vascular/CNS protection; diarrhea, nausea and headache were reported.
Mechanism does not itself establish Behçet clinical benefit; no Behçet indication in inspected US label.

after.text: In a 52-person phase 2 trial of major vascular/CNS Behçet disease, complete response at week 22 occurred in 22/27 with infliximab versus 14/25 with cyclophosphamide; both arms received glucocorticoids.
limitations: Small mixed vascular/CNS trial; no separate powered organ estimates, no global cure or long-term prevention claim. Serious adverse events: 15% versus 12%.
